newsitem.title: FINLAND: Weak bonds drag Helsinki HEX quietly below 2,900.
newsitem.headline: Weak bonds drag Helsinki HEX quietly below 2,900.

text.p: Shares fell on Tuesday as EMU jitters hurt bonds and fears of a U.S. rate hike mounted ahead of key U.S. inflation data due on Wednesday, brokers said.

Sentiment was nervous but trade thin as the 2006 bond yield rose to 6.23 percent from 6.12, and the HEX general index ended down 1.73 percent at 2,891.56, its first close below 2,900 points since March 4.

The FOX portfolio and derivatives benchmark approached suppport at 1,000 but turned up at 1,001.45 to close at 1,011.72, down 1.72 percent. Declining issues beat advancers by 90 to eight with 18 unchanged.
Brokers looked to Wall Street for support.
"The market is unlikely to collapse, but the risk for a significant fall is bigger than it used to be," one broker said, adding that "a new day on Wall Street can change everything."
"If the Dow ends one percent higher, we could have a flat day on Wednesday, if the Dow gains less than one percent, we are likely to fall," said another.
Telecoms group Nokia fell 5.90 markka to close at 310.50. accounting for 31 percent of thin 533 million markka volume. Forestry major UPM-Kymmene was second most traded, down 1.60 markka at 111.80.
Among interest rate sensitive stocks, Finland's largest banking group Merita fell on the higher bond yields but closed off a 17.40 markka low at 17.80, down 0.40 markka.

U.S. Feburary consumer prices due on Wednesday at 1330 GMT were expected to give a hint of the Federal Open Market Committee's thinking at a policy meeting due on March 25 and would set the tone for the rest of the week, brokers said.
The average forecast was for a 0.2 percent rise both in the main index and in the ex-Food/Energy index.
